title: Naturality of the explicitly constructed fixed-resolution boundary
statement: Let X,Y be schemes and f:Y→X a morphism. Let U,V be opens covering X and Uprime,Vprime opens covering Y, with Uprime=f⁻¹(U) and Vprime=f⁻¹(V). Let k:(Uprime intersection Vprime)→(U intersection V) be a scheme morphism satisfying inclusion(Uprime intersection Vprime);f=k;inclusion(U intersection V). Let F,G be abelian etale sheaves on X,Y, respectively, and phi:f^*F→G a coefficient morphism. Let I,J be injective resolutions of F,G, respectively, and cI,cJ their prescribed normalized section-homology comparisons [def-weil-pbc-etale-resolution-section-canonical-comparison]. For every degree q and intersection cohomology element x, the constructed target boundary [def-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris-canonical-boundary] applied to H.map(openSquareCoefficient(f,...,phi))(cohomologyMap(k)(x)) equals H.map(phi)(cohomologyMap(f)(the constructed source boundary applied to x)), in degree q+1. Both boundaries use the prescribed resolutions I,J and the prescribed normalized comparisons cI,cJ. This asserts one-arrow compatibility of the concrete boundaries and no exactness or simultaneous family existence. The BoundaryOn variant also accepts a specified intersection open with its equality, and gives the identical assertion after transport of that equality. The fixed-boundary specialization uses the canonical injective resolution and its normalized comparison, with no resolution input needed by callers.

source.place: Tag 0A50, injective-resolution section proof and coefficient functoriality, read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A50; Tag 01F7, resolution functoriality, read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01F7. Fixed normalized-comparison specialization written by S3.

proof.text: Obtain the section short-complex morphism with its two prescribed homology-map identities from the coefficient comparison. The covering hypotheses make both complexes short exact.

Represent the input using the source intersection equivalence, apply connecting-map naturality to its representative, and apply the target global equivalence. Substitute the two comparison identities and cancel the inverse normalized equivalences in the explicit boundary definitions.

For a specified intersection open, substitute its given equality and apply the preceding assertion. This avoids definitionally reducing a scheme restriction merely to identify its intersection presentation.
Unfold only the fixed-boundary interface and specialize the preceding proved naturality or exactness to its chosen resolution and normalized comparison.

lean.statement: theorem etaleMayerVietorisFixedBoundary_naturality {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (U V W : X.Opens) (U' V' W' : Y.Opens) (hW : W = U ⊓ V) (hW' : W' = U' ⊓ V') (hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤) (hcover' : U' ⊔ V' = ⊤) (hU : U' = f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (hV : V' = f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (k : W'.toScheme ⟶ W.toScheme) (hk : W'.ι ≫ f = k ≫ W.ι) (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (G : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (φ : (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f).obj F ⟶ G) (q : ℕ) (x : Sheaf.H ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} W.ι).obj F) q) : etaleMayerVietorisFixedBoundary U' V' W' hW' hcover' G q (Sheaf.H.map (openSquareCoefficient f W.ι W'.ι k hk F G φ) q (cohomologyMap k ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} W.ι).obj F) q x)) = Sheaf.H.map φ (q + 1) (cohomologyMap f F (q + 1) (etaleMayerVietorisFixedBoundary U V W hW hcover F q x))
